Ilok Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ilok, Croatia

Demolished. Jews came to Ilok in the 19th century from Slovakia, forming a small Yiddish-speaking Orthodox community that maintained two synagogues and a yeshiva called Hevrat Bahurim; the first synagogue, built in 1855, was rebuilt after a fire in 1873. Among the community's most notable figures was Rabbi Yosef Naftali Shtern, who had studied under the Chatam Sofer, one of the most influential halakhic authorities of the 19th century. The population reached 304 in 1921, though all of Ilok's Jewish inhabitants perished during the Holocaust; the first synagogue was abandoned in 1941 and demolished in 1948. This cemetery, built in 1869, holds 144 surviving tombstones out of 223 recorded burials as of a 2018 count, with inscriptions in Yiddish and Hebrew, and preserves the remains of the old beit tahara, now bearing a memorial to Holocaust victims.
